note: Assertions evaluated against the three real Coldcard MK4 firmware builds recorded in artifact-witness-live-captures.v1.json.gz. Those captures were produced by scripts/cloud/coldcard-build-driver.mjs inside admitted OpenAgents Cloud live_gce managed sandboxes; they are measurements, not conformance values. Every ref below is a name the driver derives from the build itself: object paths are relative to the MicroPython stm32 port build directory, and symbol names are the names the linker and nm reported.

faultMutation.description: Delete the approved hardware-TRNG provider `uint32_t rng_get(void) { return rng_get_or_fault(); }` that the fixed commit added. Nothing else changes, so a non-zero exit can only come from removing that provider.

vulnerable.description: The board configuration compiled with MICROPY_HW_ENABLE_RNG set to (0), which is the switch that routes MicroPython's stm32 rng.c into its non-hardware branch.
The linker resolved rng_get to MicroPython's own stm32 rng.o, that is, to the deterministic fallback generator rather than to the board's hardware TRNG object.
libngu's random_uint32, which supplies seed material, calls rng_get directly. The edge is a relocation in libngu/random.o, not an inference from source.

fixed.description: The guard macro is still (0) after the fix. The fix does not change the macro; it stops the upstream translation unit from providing rng_get at all.
The linker resolved rng_get to the board's own rng.o, which returns rng_get_or_fault() from the hardware TRNG.

MicroPython's stm32 rng.o contributes no symbol to the fixed link, and the fallback generator's seed state is absent from the whole enumerated inventory. This is the same condition the upstream rng-code-check target enforces, re-derived from nm output.

fault_build.description: Removing the approved provider makes the firmware link fail. The observed exit status is non-zero and no firmware image was produced.
